Same $9m story appears in Washington Post, Oct 22, 2026, 12:47 EDT, https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/10/22/pro-israel-lobby-aipac-no-longer-endorse-directly-give-candidates/. WP reports United Democracy Project (UDP), AIPAC's super PAC, gave around $9m over the preceding week to an unnamed group supporting Republican Mike Rogers; information is attributed to one person familiar with plans, anonymous before public disclosure. It does not identify recipient/entity, exact amount/date(s), transaction form or whether funds had been disbursed, booked, or ads disseminated. This is not reported as a direct $9m candidate-campaign contribution. UDP is registered FEC C00799031 as an independent-expenditure-only super PAC. FEC committee page https://www.fec.gov/data/committee/C00799031/?tab=spending states none of UDP's independent-expenditure funds are directly given to or spent by the candidate. Its summary covers receipts/disbursements through Oct 14, but detailed IE table covers only through Aug 31 and explicitly excludes 24/48-hour IE reports; linked filing view did not surface the specific reported $9m. Thus the official page cannot verify or refute this Oct 15–22 report. Independent-expenditure support for Rogers would directionally favor the held Michigan NO position (all non-Democratic outcomes, not only a Republican win), but amount-to-vote effect is unestablished and not mechanically transferable. Poll overlap unresolved: related Michigan poll headlines are dated Oct 19–21; no poll bodies/field dates were verified in this bounded pass, so cannot assess whether interviews overlapped the alleged spending week.
